Welcome
Welcome to Paxcroft Primary School
At Paxcroft Primary School, we are, ‘Proud to Belong’ and this underpins every aspectof school life. We are proud to belong to our school and the local community. We strongly believe that learning should inspire, motivate and challenge all children to achieve to their full potential. We aspire to equip all our children with the skills and knowledge they need in order to be successful in their future lives. Our caring and committed team works hard to create a safe, joyful and inclusive environment where children are encouraged to explore, dream and grow.
If you would like to come and see Paxcroft in action then please contact our office to arrange a visit.
Ashley Barrington-Wilding | Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Paxcroft Primary School - British Values Statement
pageCache.text:
British Values Statement
The DfE recently reinforced the need to "create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs."
The Government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 Prevent Strategy, and these values were reiterated in 2014. At Paxcroft Primary School these values are reinforced regularly and in the following ways. We keep an up to date audit of all such teaching and learning opportunities.
Democracy
The children have many opportunities for their voices to be heard. We have an active school council which meets regularly to discuss issues. Our school council determined our school values.
The Rule of Law
The importance of laws (rules) is reinforced throughout the curriculum as well as when discussing children's behaviour in assemblies and class-based circle time activities. Children are taught the value and reasons behind laws (rules), that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from people in positions of authority, such as the Police and Fire Service, help to reinforce this message.
Individual Liberty
Within school, the children are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. The children are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and are taught how to exercise these safely, for example, through our Online Safety and PSHE lessons. Whether it be through choice of learning challenge, of how they record their learning in books, or participation in our numerous extra-curricular clubs and opportunities, the children are given the freedom to make choices.
Mutual Respect
Mutual respect is at the heart of our values and behaviour code. The children learn that their behaviours have an effect on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community treat each other with respect.
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
Assemblies are regularly planned to address this issue either directly or through the inclusion of stories and celebrations from a variety of faiths and cultures.

About Us
Paxcroft Primary School is a welcoming 45-PAN primary school located in the heart of Trowbridge, the county town of Wiltshire. We are proud to be part of the EQUA Mead Learning Trust.
If you are considering Paxcroft for your child, we would be delighted to show you around. Please contact our school office to arrange a visit. Our team is always happy to meet prospective families, provide a tour, and answer any questions you may have.

About Us
Paxcroft Primary School is a welcoming 45-PAN primary school located in the heart of Trowbridge, the county town of Wiltshire. We are proud to be part of the EQUA Mead Learning Trust.
If you are considering Paxcroft for your child, we would be delighted to show you around. Please contact our school office to arrange a visit. Our team is always happy to meet prospective families, provide a tour, and answer any questions you may have.

Welcome
At Paxcroft, we are proud of who we are and proud of the community we belong to. Our school is a warm, inclusive and ambitious place where every child is valued, respected and supported to achieve their very best. We celebrate diversity and ensure that every pupil feels safe, welcomed and confident to be themselves.
Our ethos of “Proud to Belong” runs through everything we do. It means belonging to a community where everyone is treated fairly, where differences are respected, and where each child is encouraged to grow academically, socially and emotionally.
Our Values and Rules
Our school values and rules shape our daily life and help us create a positive, caring learning environment.
We live by our three core values: Participation: taking part, trying our best and contributing to school life
Politeness – showing kindness, good manners and consideration for others
Positivity – approaching learning and challenges with confidence and optimism
Alongside these, our three school rules guide how we behave and treat one another: Responsibility – taking ownership of our actions and learning
Respect – valuing ourselves, others and our school
Resilience – persevering, even when learning feels difficult
These values and rules help our children to become confident learners, thoughtful citizens and supportive friends.
Working Together
We believe that strong partnerships between school and home are essential. Families are a vital part of our Paxcroft community, and we warmly encourage parents and carers to get involved through events, volunteering and supporting learning at home.
By working together, we create a nurturing, inspiring environment where every child can succeed and feel truly "Proud to Belong" at Paxcroft.
Ashley Barrington-Wilding | Headteacher

Young Carers
Our school's Young Carers Operational Leads is Ashley Barrington-Wilding and can be contacted via admin@paxcroft.equamead.org or 01225 762244
Who is a young carer?
Young carers are children and young people under 18 years old who provide regular and on-going care to another person who is physically or mentally ill, disabled or misuses substances.
Many young people don’t see themselves as carers and may not realise there is practical and emotional support available in Wiltshire.
You may be a young carer if you:
need to cook for your family
help anyone to take medication regularly
translate or interpret for someone at home
The effects of being a young carer
You have responsibilities at home that prevent you from spending time with your friends, or inviting them around your house.
You feel sad, angry, guilty or embarrassed about the help you give to anyone at home.
You feel upset that friends don’t have the same responsibilities.
You avoid telling anyone outside the family about your home situation.
Where can you access the Wiltshire Young Carers Service?
Wiltshire Council's Integrated Front Door Young Carers Assessors carry out assessments of young people who care for someone else. An assessment is when an adult who works for the council gets to know the young person and the things they are dealing with to see if they need some help.
Anyone who thinks a child could be a young carer can refer the child into Wiltshire Council for a young carers' assessment.
Professionals should complete the IFD Referral Form and email to Integratedfrontdoor@wiltshire.gov.uk. Further details and a copy of the referral form can be found within our Child protection webpage.
Children and parents can self-refer into The Integrated Front Door on 0300 456 0108 or Integratedfrontdoor@wiltshire.gov.uk(opens new window)
Once the referral is received, it will be allocated to a practitioner who will contact the family and arrange a visit. The Assessment is holistic and will look at what support can be offered to the family. If the young person is deemed a young carer and their caring responsibilities are having an impact on their day-to-day lives then a referral will be made to Community First - Youth Action Wiltshire, who provide support for young carers in Wiltshire.
Further information can also be found at the council's On Your Mind website which helps young people to look after their own emotional wellbeing. It is important to let people at school know about the caring that a young person does so that they can understand and help.
Wiltshire Young Carers Service
Community First: Youth Action Wiltshire - Young Carers is the national award-winning 'youth arm' of Wiltshire based charity Community First. They work with young carers, young adult carers (aged 5 to 19), and their families in Wiltshire through a dedicated Wiltshire Young Carers Service.
Wiltshire Young Carers Service offer:
support planning and reviews
one-to-one mentoring and coaching programmes
one-to-one Time to Talk sessions
information, advice and guidance
supported signposting
help with education
skills development and nationally recognised awards

Behaviour and Relationships
At Paxcroft Primary School, we have high expectations of learning, behaviour and respect for each other and this underpins everything we do. Our team strive to create independent, articulate thinkers and learners who have the confidence to achieve their ambitions. We want all our learners to be ‘Proud to Belong’ to our school community.
At Paxcroft Primary School, we believe that Calm, Consistent and Kind adult behaviour is the foundation for good behaviour management. Calm, consistent adult behaviour means being in control of yourself before you attempt to take control of anyone else’s behaviour. Calm, consistent adult behaviour means that there are no gaps between the adults, there is an agreed plan we stick to.
At Paxcroft Primary School we are a staff team and work together, we have a tight, firm foundation. We do not shout, we do not aggress, we do not show negative emotion when intervening with behaviour.
Our school’s behaviour blueprint is built on
A clear vision
Whole school rules
Visible adult consistencies
Relentless Routines
Restorative Practice
Whole School Rules
At Paxcroft Primary School, we follow a set of simple rules which help with children’s behaviour choices, known as ‘Paxcroft’s Three Rs’. They are continually reinforced through assemblies, lunchtimes and when discussing behaviours.
Adults are responsible for discussing the school expectations with each class, with a focus on what we expect and would like to see. These will be displayed around the school for children and staff to see.
Routines are the cogs at the centre of all classroom practise. At Paxcroft Primary School, we recognise that where calm, consistent and kind routines are established, children feel secure to take risks in their learning.
We are Responsible
We are Respectful
We are Resilient
Rewards
We praise and reward children in a variety of ways. We distribute rewards to children for: following our school rules; consistent good work or behaviour; acknowledging outstanding effort or acts of kindness in school; and for excellent attendance.
Consequences
The school employs several consequences to encourage children to think about and improve their behaviour. We employ sanctions appropriately to each individual situation but try to apply them in a uniform and progressive way.

Governors
Welcome to the Paxcroft Local Governing Body page. Here you can meet the governors and find out more about the role they play within the structure and process at Paxcroft Primary School.
The Governing Body is made up of volunteers from the parent body, the staff and the wider community. The over-arching aim is to create the best possible education for our pupils and working environment for our staff. We help in developing the strategic direction of the school, whilst also monitoring and evaluating the work of the school itself.

Maths
At Paxcroft, we believe that mathematics provides essential knowledge and skills that children need for everyday life and future learning. Our aim is for all pupils to develop confidence, fluency and enjoyment in mathematics, enabling them to think mathematically and apply their knowledge to a range of problems.
Through high-quality teaching and carefully planned learning experiences, we ensure that children develop secure foundations in number, calculation and mathematical reasoning.
Our Approach to Maths
Our mathematics curriculum is designed to help children:
Develop fluency in number and calculation
Reason mathematically by explaining and justifying their thinking
Solve problems using a range of strategies
Lessons encourage children to explore ideas, make connections and develop a deep understanding of mathematical concepts.
Teachers use a structured scheme to support planning while maintaining the professional autonomy to adapt learning to meet the needs of their class.
Building Strong Number Foundations
Developing strong number sense is a key focus throughout the school.
Using Mastering Number, children learn to:
Understand number relationships
Use efficient calculation strategies
Develop mental maths skills
Apply their knowledge to solve problems
By securing these foundations, pupils are able to build confidence and tackle increasingly complex mathematical ideas.
Times Tables
Rapid recall of times tables is an important part of mathematical fluency.
At Paxcroft we provide regular opportunities for children to practise their times tables through engaging activities and digital platforms such as TT Rock Stars.
This helps children develop the quick recall needed to support wider mathematical learning.
Pupils in Year 4 take part in the national Multiplication Tables Check, which assesses their recall of multiplication facts.
Mathematical Thinking
We encourage pupils to talk about their mathematical thinking and explain their reasoning. Through discussion, questioning and problem-solving activities, children learn to:
Explain how they solved a problem
Compare different strategies
Make connections between mathematical ideas
This helps deepen understanding and supports long-term learning.
Mathematics in the Early Years
In the Early Years, mathematics is taught through a combination of adult-led activities and carefully planned provision.
Counting and number recognition
Comparing quantities
Shape, space and measure
Mathematical language through play
These experiences provide the firm foundations for learning and flourishing as children move into Key Stage 1.
Supporting Maths at Home
Parents and carers can support their child’s mathematical development by:
Practising number facts and times tables
Playing number games
Talking about maths in everyday situations such as shopping, cooking or measuring
Working together helps children build confidence and develop a positive attitude towards mathematics.

Admissions
Applications
Applications for entry to our Reception class for September 2026 open on 1st September 2025.
The school’s Published Admission Number (PAN) for September 2026 is 45.
By law, a child does not have to start school until the term following their fifth birthday. However, most children start school in the September following their fourth birthday.
If your child was born between 1st September 2021 and 31st August 2022 they are due to start school in September 2026 and you will need to apply for a school place by midnight on 15th January 2026. All children will be offered a full time place but, if you would prefer your child to attend part-time, or to delay entry until later on in the academic year, please contact the school directly to arrange this. All admissions are administered by the Local Authority.
You can apply by completing an application online with Wiltshire Council. If you do not live within Wiltshire, you must complete the common application form which is produced by your home local authority, even if you wish to apply for a place at a Wiltshire school.
During April 2026 letters will be sent out to all parents who submitted a paper application form by the January deadline, offering a place at one school. Alternatively, if you applied online you will be able to log back into the online system on national offer date to view the outcome of your application.
For our admissions policy please follow this link.
Appeals
If the Local Authority is unable to offer your child a place at Woodborough after considering your case carefully, you have the right to appeal. Appeals will be heard in late June/early July.
Late Applications
If you apply after the deadline of 15th January 2026 your application will not be considered until all of those applications received before the deadline have been processed.
Second round applications are applications received between 16th January 2026 and 26th April 2026. Applicants will receive a decision on their application around the end of May 2026.
Third round applications are applications received after 26th April and they will not be considered until after 30th June 2026. Applications received after 23rd April will be considered in date order of receipt. Decisions on third round applications will be made and posted out as soon as possible after 30th June 2026.
Applications for all Other Year Groups
If you wish to apply for a place in any year group other than Reception, please contact the School Office initially, to see if any places are available. If they are, we would be pleased to arrange a visit and you will then need to complete a separate admission application form through the Local Authority. There is no deadline for these applications. They are processed throughout the year by the Local Authority in the order in which they are received and by 31st August each year.
Parents can only hold one offer. Therefore, if an offer is made to a child during the second or third round of allocations any offer made in an earlier round will automatically be withdrawn.
Secondary School Applications
If you have a Year 6 child who is leaving us in July 2026, you can apply for a secondary school place from 1st September 2025. The closing date is midnight on 31st October 2025. You can apply online at www.wiltshire.gov.uk or complete an application form, which can be obtained on the Wiltshire Council website.
Questions
Please contact the School Office (by emailing admin@paxcroft.equamead.org) if you are interested in spaces in particular year groups, or if you have any questions about the admissions process in general or visit the Wiltshire Council website, www.wiltshire.gov.uk, which has very comprehensive information on all aspects of admissions.
Find out more about starting at Paxcroft by visiting our New Starters page.

Lunches
At Paxcroft Primary, we are proud to offer our students fresh, tasty lunches that are prepared on site every day. We understand the importance of nutritious meals for growing children, and our dedicated team works hard to ensure that every dish is both delicious and healthy. For a cost of just £2.50 per meal, we provide a variety of choices that cater to different dietary needs and preferences, ensuring that every child enjoys a satisfying lunchtime experience.

pageCache.text:
Paxcroft Community Larder
Our school community recognises that families may be struggling financially due to the current cost of living crisis.
Here at Paxcroft we are Proud to Belong! With this in mind, we have set up a Paxcroft Community Larder where families can donate and collect food and basic toiletries, as needed.
We now need to stock our Paxcroft Community Larder so if you are able to help us with donations, we would be very grateful. We are hoping for donations of long life/dry foods e.g., rice, pasta, flour, sugar, cereal, tinned foods- the sort of foods that you might normally donate for Harvest Festival. We would also appreciate donations of toiletries, snacks and treats such as biscuits, crisps, popcorn and chocolate etc.
Please note that all items donated MUST be unopened, and in date.
Accessing our Paxcroft Community Larder
Parents can donate to or collect from the Paxcroft Community Larder daily on school days between 8.30am – 4.00pm. Please note, it is your responsibility to check the ‘use by dates’ on any items you take. We have acquired a storage cabinet to use as our larder, and this is currently located outside the staff entrance, by the steps near the Slow playground.

pageCache.pageTitle: Paxcroft Primary School - Paxcroft School Association
pageCache.text:
Paxcroft School Association
Paxcroft School Association (PSA) is a charity set up to raise money to enrich the school experience for all children at Paxcroft. We can provide things that the standard school budget cannot stretch to and give opportunities to bring our school community together.
Successful events have included Christmas and Summer Fayres, discos, movie mornings, bake sales, treasure hunts, craft afternoons, bingo and the popular ice-cream Fridays in Summer!
We have also raised money for the Key Stage 1 pirate ship, Key Stage 2 adventure trail, seating around the school grounds, playground toys, speakers and lighting for productions, as well as library books and atlases. We also provide gifts for the Year 6 leavers.
All families are automatically PSA members and volunteers are always welcomed for organising or helping at events. The Annual General Meeting each October is where elections are held to form the committee, and to plan the coming year’s activities.
The PSA Facebook page is a good source of information about fundraising initiatives: https://www.facebook.com/groups/PaxcroftPSA
Ongoing activities include our successful nearly-new uniform stall – a chance to snap up good quality bargains, either at table-top sales, or through our Facebook page.
Funds can also be raised during routine online shopping, at no cost to you, by signing up to Easy Fundraising, and Amazon Smile. They donate a percentage from sales to the PSA, so please encourage friends and family to sign up via the following links:
Easy Fundraising: www.easyfundraising.org.uk/causes/paxcroftschoolassociation/
Amazon Smile: https://smile.amazon.co.uk/ch/281825-0
PSA activities are a great way to make new friends and to contribute to school life, so if you would like to get involved, or have any suggestions for future events, please email us on paxcroftpsa@gmail.com
